key_highlights: ASX ends the week net higher following an $80b post-US midterms relief rally and lower oil prices, despite late-week softening.
Department store giant David Jones enters voluntary administration after failed landlord talks, signaling severe consumer discretionary distress.
Tech and infrastructure outperform with NextDC (NXT.AX) surging on AI tailwinds, while NAB slides amid credit and margin concerns.
Qantas (QAN.AX) flags a $1B fuel expense surge, driving plans to lift airfares and trim flight capacities.
Persistent inflation and RBA rhetoric highlighting excess demand keep pressure on mortgage holders and housing valuations.

sectors.trend: Severe downturn culminated in David Jones entering administration with store closures, landlord disputes, and unpaid supplier claims.
sectors.implications: Downside risks for discretionary retail peers (PMV.AX) and re-leasing headwinds for retail landlords (SCG.AX, VCX.AX).

sectors.trend: Strong institutional demand for AI and data centre infrastructure supports listed leaders (NXT.AX), contrasting private tech layoffs (Canva).
sectors.implications: Secular AI compute growth continues to drive capital deployment; selective focus warranted on mission-critical digital infrastructure.

sectors.trend: NAB shares dropped despite broader index gains as macro headwinds, rate pressures, and potential housing loan stress weigh on bank valuations.
sectors.implications: Potential net interest margin compression and deteriorating asset quality warrant a cautious stance across major lenders (NAB.AX, CBA.AX).

sectors.trend: Resilient capital market activity across precious metals and early-stage lithium and gold exploration (BPM Minerals, Chalice, Kuniko).
sectors.implications: Junior explorers offering tactical drilling catalysts, while bulk miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX) remain tied to global demand and stimulus expectations.

sectors.trend: Crude oil declines ease general economic cost pressures, but Qantas absorbs a $1B fuel cost shock requiring flight cuts and fare hikes.
sectors.implications: Aviation margins face dual squeeze from rising unit costs and price-sensitive travelers, weighing on QAN.AX near-term free cash flow.

sectors.trend: Retail landlord lease certainty disrupted by department store insolvency; residential market faces affordability and borrowing capacity headwinds.
sectors.implications: Retail REIT distributions face lease restructuring friction; residential developers face softening buyer inquiry.

key_themes: Macro bifurcation: resilient global tech/relief rally vs acute domestic retail distress
Cost of living and rate-driven contraction impacting consumer discretionary solvency
Corporate cost inflation in aviation and logistics squeezing operating margins
Housing market vulnerability under constrained household borrowing capacity
RBA tightening cycle overhang as inflation and excess demand remain stubborn

risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight retail and apparel discretionary; reallocate toward non-cyclical consumer staples (WOW.AX, COL.AX).
Trim overweight exposure in major banks (NAB.AX, WBC.AX); favor well-capitalized institutions with low credit risk.
Maintain exposure to cash, short-duration floating rate instruments, and high-quality infrastructure assets.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Aviation Input Cost Inflation & Capacity Rationalisation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce holdings in Qantas (QAN.AX); monitor jet fuel crack spreads and consumer travel booking volumes.

opportunities.recommendation: Accumulate NextDC on AI and cloud capacity expansion
opportunities.rationale: High structural growth in enterprise data compute provides earnings resilience independent of domestic consumer cycles.

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical allocations to gold and critical mineral exploration
opportunities.rationale: Active broker underwriting and exploration discoveries provide asymmetric upside catalysts.
Household budget tightening drives grocery basket priority over discretionary retail spending.

defensive_moves.rationale: NAB's divergence and warning signs in borrowing capacity elevate risks of rising credit losses.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge ASX 200 exposure against domestic recessionary risks
defensive_moves.rationale: Domestic economic slowdown and insolvency spillovers could reverse recent midterms relief rally.

market_outlook.short_term: Range-bound ASX 200 (^AXJO) as US political risk relief is tempered by banking softness and retail insolvency headlines.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautious multi-quarter outlook as restrictive monetary policy, reduced household borrowing capacity, and housing correction risks test corporate earnings.
key_catalysts: RBA cash rate decisions and commentary regarding inflation and excess demand
